name: Imperial College London
summary: Science, engineering, medicine and business in South Kensington, London; 73 undergraduate courses, many needing HL Maths and an admissions test.

ib.text: 38–42 points overall with 6–7 in the relevant HL subjects; many courses ask 7 in HL Maths. English A at grade 4 (SL or HL), or English B at SL 6 or HL 5, meets the English requirement.

programmes.name: Aeronautical Engineering
programmes.about: An integrated master's on how vehicles and structures interact with air: aerodynamics, structures, flight mechanics, propulsion and control. Year two includes a flight-testing course at Cranfield; a year abroad or a year in industry can be added.
programmes.ib: 40 points with 7 in HL Maths and 7 in HL Physics; Maths AA is preferred over AI. Typical offers ran from 43 to 44 points.

needs.note: AA is preferred; AI is accepted

programmes.selectionNote: ESAT with Maths 1, Maths 2 and Physics (Oct or Jan sitting); selected applicants have a 25-30 minute interview with academic staff.

flagshipSource.title: Aeronautical Engineering MEng: flight testing at Cranfield, with year abroad and year in industry options

programmes.name: Medicine
programmes.about: A six-year integrated course that ends in both an MBBS and a BSc. You meet patients and clinical skills early, do research in phase two, and can follow specialist pathways such as neuroscience or mental health. Teaching is across north and west London campuses and NHS partners.
programmes.ib: 38 points with 6 in HL Biology and 6 in HL Chemistry; typical offers are 39 points with 6 or 7 in those two. Both Maths courses are accepted.
programmes.selectionNote: UCAT sat by 24 Sep 2026; scores help shortlist for Multiple Mini Interviews, from December. About a third of applicants are interviewed.

flagshipSource.title: Medicine MBBS/BSc: early clinical skills, specialist pathways and London NHS partners across several campuses

programmes.name: Chemistry
programmes.about: Core and applied chemistry to master's level: inorganic, organic, physical, analytical, synthetic and computational, with an extensive laboratory programme. It ends in a six-month research project in an academic group; year-in-industry and year-abroad versions exist.
programmes.ib: 38 points with 6 in HL Chemistry, 6 in HL Maths and 6 in a third HL subject (Biology, Economics or Physics preferred). Typical offers are 39 to 40 points.

needs.note: No preference between AA and AI
Third HL at 6; these three are preferred

programmes.selectionNote: No admissions test. Predicted grades, personal statement and reference are read; shortlisted applicants have an academic interview, with decisions by early March.

flagshipSource.title: Chemistry MSci: a laboratory programme and a six-month research project in an academic group

faculties.name: Faculty of Engineering
faculties.line: Most departments set the ESAT, Computing the TMUA; Bioengineering, Earth Science, Materials none. Aeronautics: 7s in HL Maths, Physics.

faculties.name: Faculty of Natural Sciences
faculties.line: Chemistry has no test; Mathematics takes the TMUA, Physics and Life Sciences the ESAT. Chemistry asks HL 6s in Chemistry and Maths.

faculties.name: Faculty of Medicine
faculties.line: Medicine closes 15 October: UCAT, then interviews; HL Biology and Chemistry at 6. BSc Medical Biosciences uses no test.

faculties.name: Imperial College Business School
faculties.line: Economics, Finance and Data Science: TMUA compulsory; 39 points with 7 in HL Maths and 6 in two more HL subjects.

notes: ESAT is needed for engineering, physics and life sciences, TMUA for computing, maths and the Business School, and UCAT for Medicine.
You may sit ESAT in October or January, but only your first score counts.
Overseas fees are set per course: Mathematics BSc cost £42,700 in 2026-27, and 2027 figures were not yet out.
